name: Felipe VI of Spain
summary: Felipe VI is a constitutional monarch who, in his speeches, defends the 1978 Constitution, the parliamentary monarchy and the unity of Spain, while recognising its territorial and linguistic diversity. He backs European integration, the UN-centred rules-based order, the Atlantic alliance and a welfare state, and speaks against extremism and polarisation. His speeches are delivered within the constitutional role and with the government's countersignature, so his recorded positions on contested policy questions are sparse.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Has described public services such as health and education as essential and, in his 2026 European Parliament speech, said that in the Europe he wants education and health care are rights; he did not speak of a specific universal-coverage scheme.

cut-welfare.rationale: Repeatedly asks for a solid welfare state and protection of vulnerable groups; has not addressed the dependency argument directly.

social-market-economy.rationale: In Strasbourg in 2015 he quoted Delors in rejecting a Europe that is only a market without a social dimension, and in 2026 said freedom and social cohesion go hand in hand; he also backs a social and democratic state governed by rule of law.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Says the crisis left people injured in their dignity, that protecting the most vulnerable and fighting inequality is a matter of dignity, and that the state has a duty to protect the most vulnerable families.

women-suffrage.rationale: Called for women to take part on a par with men in working life and in exercising political and social rights, and speaks of eliminating discrimination and strengthening women's role.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Says human dignity is not negotiable, that the UN Charter and Universal Declaration apply to all, and in 2026 spoke of one humanity regardless of colour, faith and origin.

universal-morality.rationale: At the UN he argued for the universality of the Charter and human rights principles against particularism and relativism and described rules as the voice of reason in international relations.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Urges honouring what makes Spaniards who they are, including shared culture, history and the co-official languages, and speaks of the Constitution protecting the traditions and cultures of Spain's peoples.

minority-language-support.rationale: In 2014 said the other languages of Spain are a common heritage that the Constitution requires be treated with special respect and protection; he did not mention schools or elections specifically.

single-official-language.rationale: Noted Castilian is the state's official language while insisting the other languages are a shared heritage to be protected and respected, not suppressed.

gradual-change.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

death-penalty.rationale: At the UN in 2025 named eradicating the death penalty among the causes Spain pursues on the Human Rights Council.

state-harmful.rationale: Praises the soundness of the Spanish state and the social and democratic state of law as the guarantee of coexistence and public services; speaks of a state with duties to protect citizens.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Stated in 2014 his conviction that the parliamentary monarchy can and should keep serving Spain through its independence, neutrality and integrating role, and has reigned on that basis since.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succeeded his father on the throne in 2014 and has staged and affirmed the succession line to his daughter, speaking of her oath as continuing the Monarchy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inherited the throne and defends the parliamentary monarchy as the head of state rather than an elected presidency.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Described the Crown's independence, political neutrality and integrating role towards the different ideological options as its function, and the King as symbol of unity and permanence of the state.

separated-powers.rationale: Stated that the King must respect the separation of powers, obey the laws passed by the Cortes and respect judicial independence, and repeated that separation and independence are pillars of democracy.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Said the King must comply with the laws passed by the Cortes and that each institution, beginning with the King, must stay within its constitutional place and obligations.

democracy-best.rationale: Frames liberal democracy and the rule of law as the basis of coexistence, warns of erosion of democracies and says outside the Constitution there is no democracy or freedom.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said sovereignty rests in the Spanish people and the Cortes represent it with full legitimacy, and that the Crown must earn citizens' trust to hold moral authority.

one-party-rule.rationale: Defends political pluralism as a constitutional value and democratic coexistence under a parliamentary system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Insists the 1978 Constitution be defended, respected and preserved in its identity while open to reform within it; no mention of a new constituent process.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

right-to-secede.rationale: In his 3 October 2017 address called the Catalan government's attempt to declare independence illegal and an attempt to break national unity and sovereignty, and has repeated his commitment to the unity and permanence of Spain.

national-self-determination.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

collective-defense.rationale: Spoke of reinforcing collective defence with allies, of strengthening the European pillar within the Atlantic Alliance, and said weakening the transatlantic alliance would hurt every member's security.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Backs strengthening alliances and Spain's NATO and transatlantic commitments.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Describes Spain's commitment to the transatlantic alliance and the NATO summit hosted in Madrid in 2022 as a strengthening of the Alliance.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Calls for stronger European defence and strategic autonomy and praises Spain's armed forces; wants defence capability kept.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

return-lost-territory.rationale: At the UN he repeatedly urges the United Kingdom to end Gibraltar's colonial status through a negotiated solution restoring Spain's territorial integrity.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Describes Ibero-America as a community of brother nations tied by history and language, wants to potentiate those ties and hosts the Ibero-American Summit.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wants a stronger, more integrated and united Europe and says Spain recognizes itself fully in building the united European space.

close-ties-china.rationale: Made a state visit to China as part of a comprehensive strategic partnership while calling the transatlantic link strategic and essential; both ties are affirmed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: At the UN described properly managed immigration as a vector of mutual development and backed the global migration and refugee compacts; in 2024 warned poorly managed migration can strain cohesion but did not call to reduce levels.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate action a major issue and in 2025 urged triple renewable capacity, doubling of energy efficiency and decarbonisation, saying doubts must be left aside.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Backs accelerated just energy transition and continued decarbonisation of economies.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Committed at the UN to end extreme poverty, said Spain has increased contributions to international development funds and urges addressing the Agenda 2030 financing gap.

future-generations.rationale: Frames climate and environment as matters of the planet's future and legacy owed to coming generations, without a specific statement on handing on the Earth undamaged.

political-violence-never.rationale: Honours victims of terrorism, hatred and violence and has said democracy depends on settling differences within the law and without violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Describes war as horror and devastation that disregards life and dignity, and says force without principle amounts to barbarism.

notes: As a constitutional monarch his formal assent to laws (e.g. on abortion, same-sex marriage, the 2024 amnesty law) is not his position and is not used. Speeches abroad and on state occasions are delivered with ministers' endorsement, so statements on foreign policy are rated medium at most. Personal measures counted only as record on succession and household transparency (renouncing any inheritance from his father in 2020 and publishing his assets in 2022, per Wikipedia).
